reports.title: Taysha Gene Therapies Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Corporate Update

desk.headline: No revenue; net loss $0.10 a share, narrower than the -$0.125 estimate; Rett syndrome pivotal data and FDA filing-path feedback due 1H 2027

numbers.eps_basis: GAAP net loss per share, basic and diluted

other.label: Patients dosed with TSHA-102
other.change: no severe treatment-related SAEs or DLTs

results: Taysha is a clinical-stage gene therapy company with no product sales; the quarter's net loss widened to $39.1m ($0.10 a share) from $32.7m ($0.09).
Spending rose as trials ran and launch preparation began: R&D up $3.1m to $28.8m, overhead up $4.8m to $13.1m.
All 33 patients dosed with TSHA-102 for Rett syndrome have passed the early safety window with no severe treatment-related serious side effects or dose-limiting toxicities.
The commercial-scale manufacturing validation run (PPQ) needed for an FDA filing was completed and met all preset specifications.
Cash of $422.8m is expected to fund the company into the second half of 2028.

guidance.summary: As a pre-revenue biotech, Taysha gives no sales or profit guidance. It expects its cash to last into the second half of 2028 and lists key milestones for the first half of 2027.

items.metric: REVEAL pivotal 6-month interim topline data and FDA feedback on filing path
FDA feedback after manufacturing (CMC) Type B meeting

points: The six-month interim analysis is triggered when the last patient hits six months in December 2026; roughly a third of patients need to respond.
Management will ask the FDA about filing on six-month data, which could save at least two quarters versus waiting for 12-month data; the FDA has not given a view yet.
Commercial, medical and payer-access teams are being built; early payer feedback was described as positive and a commercial supply deal is in place.
On safety questions, management said MRI monitoring showed no tumour signals; one patient had a moderate (grade 2) nerve side effect and was recovering.
The company plans to stay quiet from January until it meets the FDA on the interim data.
